description: Where the Blind Spot Lies — An Examination of Security Through a Scam Case Ilhun Cardano Mainnet has never been penetrated until now. The Ouroboros consensus has operated normally, and off-chain settlements have not been disrupted. However, when you open the “Report a Scam” board on the Karadao forum, similar titles appear monthly. Titles like "My ADA disappeared from my wallet" or "I didn't touch anything, but it's gone." How do you understand this contradiction? The protocol is fine, but people's assets continue to disappear. The problem always seems to occur at "the seam." In my previous security series, we touched on the fact that the periphery of the Cardano ecosystem, including bridges, hardware wallets, signature interfaces, and interchain protocols, serves as the structural blind spot.

title: Safe Wallets but Why Do Money Vanish? — Report on the Shadows ① | Security
description: Safe wallets but why do money vanish? — Report on the Shadows ① This is the first article in a series that examines five recurring points of damage observed in the periphery of the Cardano ecosystem. Ilhun Cardano Mainnet has never been hacked. Neither the Ouroboros consensus algorithm, nor the on-chain settlement has been a problem. Yet, opening the forum's 'Report a Scam' board reveals recurring posts titled, 'ADA vanished from my wallet.' 'I did not press any button.' Contradicting the protocol, assets are vanishing despite the blockchain being secure. The solution is surprisingly simple. The issue lies not within the chain itself, but at the intersection of the chain and the people — specifically, the gap between wallet applications and how they store data on devices.
